title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. On the previous pages Grothendieck tried to define a refinement of a figure (a configuration of strata in a 'pseudo-disc' or tame space) elementwise: F' refines F if every stratum X' in F' refines some stratum X in F. Here he decides this is badly behaved. He makes 'subdivision of a figure' the primitive notion, and defines 'refinement of a figure' as a sub-figure of a subdivision. He then announces a 'nouveau départ!' and begins an axiomatic framework.

Definition. A 'contrée' C is a triple (M, F, Σ).
- M is a set, whose elements he calls multistrates (multi-strata).
- F ⊂ P(M) is a family of subsets of M, called figures. The margin says that if F ∈ F, the elements X ∈ F are called the multistrata of F.
- Σ is a binary relation on F, read 'F' is a subdivision of F'.

Axiom C1. For every X ∈ M there is a smallest figure F_X containing X, called the elementary figure defined by X.

Axiom C'1. F_X ≠ F_Y whenever X ≠ Y, i.e. X ↦ F_X is injective.

The order. Define X ≤ Y iff F_X ⊂ F_Y, equivalently X ∈ F_Y. A footnote insists this should be a genuine order and not merely a preorder; that is the purpose of C'1.

Modern reading. M is a poset of 'cells' or strata. F_X is the closure of the cell X, and ≤ is the face (specialisation) order. The next page shows that every figure is a lower set for ≤. It then adds:
- a compatibility axiom C2: F ∪ G is a figure iff its elements are pairwise compatible;
- an axiom C3: every lower subset of a figure is a figure (sub-figures).

So a contrée is a T0 Alexandrov-type space (closed sets = figures, partially defined unions) equipped with an abstract subdivision relation. It is an axiomatisation of the combinatorics of stratified tame spaces and their subdivisions, serving the 'analysis situs' / tame-topology programme. The aim is to set up a purely combinatorial theory where subdivision, not elementwise refinement, is the basic operation, as in PL topology.
errors: No mathematical error. Minor redundancy: C1 already gives X ∈ F_Y ⇔ F_X ⊂ F_Y (by minimality), so ≤ is automatically a preorder; C'1 is exactly what makes it antisymmetric, as the footnote says.
Σ is introduced but no axioms on it are given on this page. Its interaction with figures (e.g. transitivity, compatibility with sub-figures) remains to be specified.

ideas.what: Replace elementwise 'refinement' of figures by a primitive notion of 'subdivision'; define a refinement as a sub-figure of a subdivision.
ideas.modern_name: Subdivision as primitive (PL topology / abstract subdivision of cell complexes; refinement = subcomplex of a subdivision)
ideas.where_published: Only general motivation for tame topology in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'contrée' (M, F, Σ): set of multistrata, family of figures with smallest figure F_X through each point, injectivity, induced face order.
ideas.modern_name: Abstract cell complex / face poset with Alexandrov (T0) closure structure plus a subdivision relation; cf. stratified spaces, exit-path posets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Tucker (1933), Alexandroff (1937) for discrete/Alexandrov spaces; Kovalevsky abstract cell complexes (1980s)
ideas.where_published: unpublished (this manuscript); Esquisse d'un programme only sketches tame topology

missed.claim: An axiomatic combinatorial 'tame topology' in which spaces are posets of strata with a family of figures and a primitive subdivision relation Σ. It anticipates a framework comparing different stratified models up to subdivision, but the Σ-axioms are not developed here.
missed.quote: il vaut mieux prendre comme une notion primitive celle de subdivision d'une figure ... Donc, nouveau départ! Une contrée C est définie par un triple (M, F, Σ)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to combinatorial models of stratified spaces (exit-path categories, posets of strata, o-minimal cell decompositions) where invariance under subdivision is central. It is a concrete trace of how Grothendieck intended to realise the tame-topology programme of the Esquisse, though the content on this page is elementary.

missed.claim: Together with the next page (compatibility via pairwise compatibility, lower-closed sub-figures), the figure structure is essentially a binary-coherent family of down-sets. This resembles coherence spaces and event structures, developed independently in computer science around the same time.
missed.quote: X ≤ Y ⇔ F_X ⊂ F_Y i.e. X ∈ F_Y et on trouve une relation d'ordre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a mild structural parallel only, unlikely to be significant.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an interesting unpublished trace of Grothendieck axiomatising tame topology via a 'contrée' with subdivision as primitive. But the actual content on this page (T0 poset from minimal closed sets) is elementary and closely parallels known abstract cell complex / Alexandrov space notions.
transcription_corrections: 'ens. des multi-structures' should read 'ens. des multi-strates' (the line break gives 'multi-' / 'strates)'). Likewise the margin reads 'les X ∈ F sont dits (multistrates) de F', and '(qui est à nouveau ... ; celle d'une multistrate)' rather than 'multistructure'.
The word transcribed 'raffinement[?]' is written in abbreviated form 'r. ffinement'; the reading 'raffinement' is plausible.
The insertion above 'plus petite' in C1 seems to mention an intersection of figures containing X (justifying the 'smallest' figure), not 'F ⊃ tous les éléments de M'. It is only partly legible.
C'1: the insertion reads approximately 'i.e. F_X ≠ F_Y si X ≠ Y', i.e. X ↦ F_X injective; the '∃F∈F t.q.' prefix is likely a misreading of crossed-out text.
